Shiva. The destroyer and transformer of the Hindu trinity, embodying the cycles of death, renewal, and cosmic destruction necessary for creation to begin anew.

Shiva is the third member of the Trimurti, responsible for the dissolution and transformation of the cosmos. He is depicted with a third eye on his forehead, his body covered with ash, and a serpent coiled around his neck—Vasuki, the divine serpent. He holds a trident, the trishul, and a damaru, a small drum. These symbolize cosmic creation and destruction.

Parvati is his consort, and together they are parents to Ganesha and Kartikeya, also called Murugan. Shiva is considered the supreme yogi, dwelling in meditation on Mount Kailash, the cosmic axis of the universe. His tandava, his cosmic dance, represents the cycles of creation and destruction that govern all existence.

Shaivism is one of the major branches of Hinduism, centered on devotion to Shiva. The lingam, a stone pillar, is his primary symbol and the focal point of Shiva worship in temples throughout the world.

Shiva represents the ultimate force that dissolves the universe at the end of each cosmic age, allowing for renewal and rebirth. Through his meditative power and his transformative dance, he embodies the principle that destruction and renewal are essential to all cosmic cycles.
